instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1/2-inch cubes.
Quarter the tomatoes. Blend them with half the onion, the garlic and a splash of water until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high. Pour in the blended tomato mixture. Stand back, it will spatter. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.
Add the potatoes, the broth, 2 cups water, the oregano, 3 sprigs of the cilantro and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat.
Reduce to a steady simmer and cook for 12 minutes, until a potato cube mashes easily against the side of the pot.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro leaves. Taste the soup, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Ladle into bowls and top with the chopped cilantro.
method_notes: Mexican Food Journal leads (4.25 from 32): fry blended tomatoes with onion, then simmer potatoes in water and tomato until tender. Alecooks does the same with a blended tomato, onion and garlic base fried until deep red, oregano and a cilantro sprig, and finishes in 20 minutes. This follows the lead's 6 cups of liquid and tomato-to-potato ratio, with the faster blended base from Alecooks and 1/2-inch cubes in place of the lead's strips, which need 30 minutes. The lead's chicken bouillon is replaced with vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian. It is a brothy tomato soup, not a creamy one as the list line says. About 34 minutes in all, a little over 30.
